newsitem.title: USA: Senate sets debate on chemical weapons treaty.
newsitem.headline: Senate sets debate on chemical weapons treaty.

text.p: The Senate agreed on Thursday to open debate next Wednesday on an international treaty outlawing chemical weapons.
Under a schedule formally adopted by the Senate, the debate will last at least 16 hours and will include votes on amendments that treaty supporters say will torpedo U.S. participation in the treaty.

Final vote on the global Chemical Weapons Convention was expected to take place next week. The Clinton administration is lobbying hard for Senate approval of the treaty before April 29, when it goes into effect with or without the United States. The schedule appeared to allow for ratification before the deadline.
The treaty, signed by 161 nations and ratified by 70, bans the development, production, stockpiling, transfer and use of chemical weapons. Its approval requires a two-thirds majority of the Senate.

The unanimous consent agreement on the treaty debate was announced by Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott, and followed intensive negotiations with Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chairman Jesse Helms, a North Carolina Republican and implacable foe of the treaty.

Meanwhile, the Senate began debate on a separate bill under which the United States would take a go-it-alone role in combating the spread of chemical and biological weapons. It bans such weapons within the United States and provides for U.S. sanctions against other countries using them.
